Let the necessary correction be impleaded in the prayer clause within the course of the day.
Counter affidavit filed by learned counsel for the opposite party No. 2 is taken on record.
Heard learned counsel for the revisionist, learned counsel for the opposite party No. 2., learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.

The instant criminal revision has been preferred by the revisionist against the impugned order dated 06.06.2023 passed by Additional Sessions Judge, Court No. 2, Gorakhpur in S.T. No. 1934 of 2022 (State Vs. Raj Chauhan) in Case Crime No. 258 of 2022, under Sections 498A, 323, 504, 506, 304-B IPC and Section 3/4 of the D.P. Act, Police Station-Gulriya, District-Gorakhpur, whereby his application for declaration of juvenile has been rejected.

sentences.text: The said Certificate does not conform to the provision of Section 94 of the Juvenile Justice Act, 2015, as the said certificate is neither of the matriculation or equivalent certificate from the concerned examination Board nor it has been disclosed by the guardian of the revisionist as to what basis the said date of birth has been entered nor school records or the Certificate of the school first attended has been produced.
Even the criteria of second preference of Section 94 could not fulfill as no birth certificate from the Municipal Corporation or Nagar Palika or Nagar Panchayat is available.
Per contra, learned A.G.A. could not dispute the aforesaid submission.

Section 94 of the Juvenile Justice Act, 2015 provides as follows:
"(1) Where, it is obvious to the Committee or the Board, based on the appearance of the person brought before it under any of the provisions of this Act (other than for the purpose of giving evidence) that the said person is a child, the Committee or the Board shall record such observation stating the age of the child as nearly as may be and proceed with the inquiry under section 14 or section 36, as the case may be,
without waiting for further confirmation of the age.
(2) In case, the Committee or the Board has reasonable grounds for doubt regarding whether the person brought before it is a child or not, the Committee or the Board, as the case may be, shall undertake the process of age determination, by seeking evidence by obtaining?
(i) the date of birth certificate from the school, or the matriculation or equivalent certificate from the concerned examination Board, if available; and in the absence thereof;
(ii) the birth certificate given by a corporation or a municipal authority or a panchayat;
(iii) and only in the absence of (i) and (ii) above, age shall be determined by an ossification test or any other latest medical age determination test conducted on the orders of the Committee or the Board:
Provided such age determination test conducted on the order of the Committee or the Board shall be completed within fifteen days from the date of such order.
(3) The age recorded by the Committee or the Board to be the age of person so brought before it shall, for the purpose of this Act, be deemed to be the true age of that person".

Recently, the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Karan alias Fatiya Vs. State of Madhya Pradesh (2023) 5 SCC 504 has held that "It is in the absence of the first category of documents being not available that the birth certificate from the municipal corporation is to be considered and, thus, if under the first and second columns, documents are not available, only then reference to medical board and holding of an ossification test comes into play - Resultantly, ossification test claimed by the State by contending that the documents filed during the inquiry before trial Court were not covered under Section 94, held, not material and declined."
Considering the aforesaid facts and circumstances and the submissions made herein above as well as the case law cited, it is hereby directed that in case the revisionist appears before the Juvenile Justice Board for the medical examination/ossification test for the determination of the age, the same be conducted by a duly constituted Medical Board within a period of two months from the date of production of the certified copy of the order.
With the aforesaid direction, the criminal revision is disposed of.
